subject: Control-surface attestation & topology portability roadmap
messages:
From: Elena Gonzales <elena.gonzales@blueriver-analytics.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueRiver Security Team <security@blueriver-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: control-surface attestation + topology portability

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency profile looked promising. Our security team is preparing a SIG-lite intake and has a few follow-ups specifically about the control surface and network portability between Dedicated and Private deployments. They asked for:  

- A short attestation of which control-plane ports and protocols are required for Redwood Private vs Dedicated (e.g., ranges, TCP/UDP, mutual TLS).
- A simple topology diagram that shows the minimal set of inbound/outbound paths for a private deployment (VPC) and how a Dedicated pool would interconnect for telemetry/fallbacks.
- Notes on how portable the diagram is — i.e., if their network team needs to move from AWS to Azure on-prem appliances, what changes (routing, NAT, firewall rules) are anticipated.

Could you point us to a one-pager or produce a short roadmap for the attestation and a diagram we can share with our network team? Our legal/compliance deadline is next Friday, 2027-04-09.

Appreciate it,
Elen a

--
Elena Gonzales
Head of Procurement, BlueRiver Analytics
elena.gonzales@blueriver-analytics.com
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gonzales <elena.gonzales@blueriver-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: control-surface attestation + topology portability

Elena — thanks for the clear ask and the deadline. I can coordinate on a concise packet. Quick plan:  

1) Kimberly will draft the control-surface attestation table listing ports/protocols and whether they are required for Private, Dedicated, or both.  
2) Karthik will generate a minimal topology diagram (PDF) that highlights VPC peering, egress points, and optional Dedicated telemetry channels.  
3) I will add a portability notes section describing impact of cloud provider changes and a short checklist for network teams (NAT, IP ranges, mTLS cert rotation).

We should be able to deliver a draft by EOD 2027-04-05 so you have time for internal review ahead of Friday. Attaching a TODO and a proposed filename convention for evidence: network-portability-diagram-v1.pdf; control-surface-claim-table-v1.csv; segmentation-attestation-draft.pdf.

If BlueRiver needs signed attestation language (legal), flag that today so we can route to legal.

Best,
Rohan

--
Rohan Mehta
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
rohan.mehta@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>, Elena Gonzales <elena.gonzales@blueriver-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: control-surface attestation + topology portability

Elena / team — attaching the first-pass artifacts for BlueRiver review (see attachments). Highlights:  

- control-surface-claim-table-v1.csv: column definitions include port, protocol, direction (inbound/outbound), required_for (Private/Dedicated/Both), encryption (mTLS/TLS/none), justification, config_location (console/api).  

- network-portability-diagram-v1.pdf: two-page diagram. Page 1 shows Private deployment (VPC) with typical customer-managed firewall rules and Redwood Private control-plane egress endpoints. Page 2 shows Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU pool) with optional telemetry egress to a Redwood telemetry collector over mTLS. We've annotated the minimal port ranges: 443 (HTTPS), 9411 (optional tracing), and a short list of ephemeral ports for healthchecks. Where possible we've avoided fixed source IPs — we recommend CIDR ranges on customer side for peering.

Portability notes (inline in PDF and summarized here):  
- Moving between IaaS providers rarely changes the required ports (HTTPS + mTLS). Biggest differences are in the networking primitives: Azure uses Service Endpoints/Private Link patterns while AWS uses VPC Peering/Transit Gateway. Both require NAT/egress allowances for outbound control-plane calls.
- For on-prem appliances, the checklist includes: ensure outbound 443 to Redwood control-plane FQDNs, allow outbound mTLS to telemetry endpoint if Dedicated telemetry is enabled, and allow bi-directional BGP only if using advanced interconnects.  

Next steps:  
- If BlueRiver wants signed attestation language, I can produce a short paragraph with an authorized Redwood security signature.  
- Karthik / Mina: can you confirm the attachment file hashes and that the diagrams are redacted of any internal IPs (done) before we send final?

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Elena Gonzales <elena.gonzales@blueriver-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: BlueRiver Security Team <security@blueriver-analytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: control-surface attestation + topology portability

Thanks — this is perfect and fast. We reviewed the diagrams and the claim table; couple of follow-ups from our network lead:  

1) Can you confirm whether Dedicated telemetry uses mutual TLS with client cert rotation frequency? Our ops team requires a nominal rotation schedule for certs.
2) For the ephemeral healthcheck ports, can you provide an explicit ephemeral port range recommendation to pre-approve in our firewall team?

If you can add two short bullets in the attestation PDF answering those, we should be able to close the SIG-lite intake. No legal-signed attestation needed for now; if we need it later we'll let you know.

I’ll mark the HubSpot deal as evidence-received once we have the updated attestation.

Best,
Elena

--
Elena Gonzales
Head of Procurement, BlueRiver Analytics
[Attachments referenced: network-portability-diagram-v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages), control-surface-claim-table-v1.csv (CSV), segmentation-attestation-draft.pdf (PDF)]
